question: Using $R = R_0 A^{1/3}$, show why the density of a nucleus is nearly independent of its mass number.

options.A: Since $R\propto A^{1/3}$, volume is proportional to $A^{1/3}$ while mass is proportional to $A$, so density increases with $A^{2/3}$.
options.B: Nuclear density decreases as $1/A$ because nuclear volume is independent of $A$.
options.C: Nuclear density is zero for large nuclei because their radii are larger.
options.D: $R\propto A^{1/3}$ implies $V\propto R^3\propto A$. Nuclear mass is also proportional to $A$, so $\rho=\dfrac{\text{mass}}{\text{volume}}\propto\dfrac{A}{A}$ is nearly constant.
